claims.text: Selective internal oxidation of Ti occurs at fcc grain boundaries during high-temperature oxidizing exposure.
Grain-boundary internal oxidation governs embrittlement and catastrophic failure of the additively manufactured alloy.
Increasing Ti content by 50% promotes formation of a continuous protective Ti-rich surface oxide scale.
A continuous Ti-rich surface scale reduces oxygen penetration along grain boundaries.
Reduced grain-boundary oxygen penetration preserves ductility and strength.
The as-printed Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a single-phase fcc matrix.
The as-printed alloy has an average grain size of approximately 10 μm.
The nominal Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a baseline Ti content of 0.3 at.%.
The controlled intervention is an increase in Ti from 0.3 at.% to 0.45 at.% while holding processing parameters constant.
Higher Ti availability preferentially forms a dense TiOx layer at the surface.
The dense TiOx layer slows inward oxygen diffusion.
Slower inward oxygen diffusion suppresses internal Ti-oxide nucleation at grain boundaries.
After 100 h at 800 °C, the Ti-enriched alloy will have approximately 25% less internal-oxide penetration along grain boundaries than the baseline alloy.
After 100 h at 800 °C, the Ti-enriched alloy will have approximately 20% lower scale spallation than the baseline alloy.
After 100 h at 800 °C, the Ti-enriched alloy will retain approximately 15% higher fracture toughness than the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from 600 to 900 °C, at oxygen partial pressures of 0.01 to 1 bar, and for exposures up to 1000 h.
Direct data on Ti-rich scale continuity in this specific HEA system are limited.

contradictions.description: The nominal formula uses relative stoichiometric coefficients, not atomic percentages. Normalizing Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 gives about 5.45 at.% Ti, not 0.3 at.%; changing the Ti coefficient to 0.45 gives about 7.96 at.% Ti, not 0.45 at.%. Thus the stated compositions and the claimed 0.3-to-0.45 at.% intervention are inconsistent.
